title: Counting the Months on Which a Supplement Policy and a Medicare Advantage Enrollment Ran Together
content:
Where a policyholder under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies also held cover under Medicare Advantage Health Plans, the months on which the two coverages ran together are counted from the date that other coverage ended, read from the member's enrollment record in Medicare Advantage Health Plans, and from whether premium has been charged on the supplement since it took effect.

### The count

| The record shows | The months counted as run together |
|---|---|
| The other Medicare coverage ended in the same calendar month in which the supplement took effect, and premium has been charged since the supplement took effect | The month in which the other coverage ended is itself counted, so 1 month is returned |
| The other Medicare coverage ended in a later calendar month than the one in which the supplement took effect, and premium has been charged since the supplement took effect | The months counted run from the month the supplement took effect up to but not including the month in which the other coverage ended |
| Neither of those holds | No month is counted as run together, and premium is owed from the day the supplement took effect |

### The two limbs of each condition

Each of the first two rows is a compound condition, and both of its limbs must hold. The first limb compares the calendar month in which the other Medicare coverage ended with the calendar month in which the supplement took effect: the same month for the first row, a later month for the second. The second limb is the same in both rows — that premium has been charged on the supplement since it took effect. Where premium has not been charged since the supplement took effect, neither of the first two rows is reached whatever the two dates show, and the last row governs.

### Illustrations on hypothetical dates

Where a supplement took effect in a given month and the member's Medicare Advantage coverage ended in that same month, with premium charged since the supplement took effect, 1 month is counted.

Where a supplement took effect in one month and that other coverage ended three calendar months later, with premium charged since the supplement took effect, the months counted run from the month the supplement took effect up to but not including the month the other coverage ended, so 3 months are counted.

Where the other coverage had ended before the supplement took effect, neither of the first two rows holds and no month is counted as run together.
